security.title: Security
security.lede: A factual view of the controls available in FastAccounts, the choices self-hosters own, and the review and planned work before production rollout.

sections.title: Hosting model
sections.body: FastAccounts can be self-hosted, in which case the operator chooses and secures the infrastructure. The hosted pilot runs the same Docker application with PostgreSQL and persistent evidence storage on FastSME-managed infrastructure. The underlying hosting provider is deployment-specific and must be named in a production customer agreement.

sections.title: Encryption
sections.body: Integration credentials are encrypted at rest with a key-versioned Fernet vault and are excluded from browser responses and logs. Hosted traffic uses HTTPS/TLS. FastAccounts does not currently claim that every database field or uploaded evidence file is application-level encrypted at rest.

sections.title: Backups and recovery
sections.body: Self-hosters are responsible for their own database, evidence-storage, encryption and restore process. Planned: encrypted managed-hosting backups and tested restores. The repository does not record a completed backup-and-restore drill, so no recovery-time promise is made.

sections.title: Access control
sections.body: Available: local email/password accounts and Google sign-in, invite-only organisation membership, signed sessions, CSRF protection and owner, administrator, accountant, approver and viewer roles. Passwords use scrypt hashes; confirmation and reset tokens are single-use hashes, and repeated sign-in attempts are throttled. Business records are scoped by organisation and cross-tenant access is covered by tests. Planned: a managed-service MFA policy and edge rate limiting.

sections.title: Incidents
sections.body: Send a suspected security incident privately to info@predictivelabs.ai with “FastAccounts security incident” in the subject. The team will preserve relevant records, investigate scope and coordinate customer communication. Planned: contractual incident-response times; none are currently offered.

sections.title: Dependency reporting
sections.body: Python dependencies are declared in requirements.txt and CI compiles the application, runs tests, verifies migrations and scans committed files for common secret patterns. The project does not claim continuous automated dependency-vulnerability monitoring. Report a suspected vulnerable dependency through the private security contact.

sections.title: Responsible disclosure
sections.body: Please report vulnerabilities privately before public discussion and include affected versions, reproduction steps and impact. We will confirm a communication channel, investigate in good faith and coordinate a disclosure date with the reporter. Please allow a reasonable opportunity to remediate; response or fix deadlines are not yet guaranteed.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: This Pilot notice explains the roles and data paths visible in the current product. A customer data-processing agreement must complete the production arrangement.

sections.title: Controller and processor roles
sections.body: For a hosted service, Predictive Labs Ltd acts as controller for account, support and service-administration data, and as processor for business, customer, supplier and employee data entered by an organisation. The customer remains controller of that organisation data. In a self-hosted deployment, the operator determines its own roles and notices.

sections.title: Current subprocessors
sections.body: The current code uses Google for optional sign-in and Postmark for account, invoice and reminder email when those features are configured. Postmark is not used when its credentials are absent. The repository does not identify the managed-infrastructure provider; any production hosting provider must be named in the customer DPA before production customer data is accepted. Connected accounting, HR or banking providers are customer-directed integrations, not default recipients.

sections.title: Retention
sections.body: Accounting records are retained according to the customer’s policy and applicable statutory periods: the product roadmap records six years for ordinary UK VAT records and seven years from the end of the financial year for Estonian accounting records, with longer holds where required. Deletion requests cannot silently remove posted ledgers or records under a statutory or legal hold. Planned: automated retention execution for managed hosting.

sections.title: International transfers
sections.body: A self-hoster chooses its data location. In the hosted pilot, Google or Postmark may process data under their own service terms and transfer safeguards. The production DPA must record the hosting location, every subprocessor and any transfer mechanism; this page does not invent a location that is not documented in the repository.

sections.title: Analytics and logs
sections.body: The public site and application contain no analytics or advertising SDK. A deployment may keep operational web, authentication and audit logs needed to run and secure the service. Those logs must not contain provider credentials, and their retention must be documented for production hosting.

sections.title: Data-subject requests
sections.body: For access, correction, deletion, restriction or another data-protection request, first contact the organisation that controls the relevant books. For FastAccounts account or service data, email info@predictivelabs.ai. We may need to verify identity and preserve records that must legally remain.

about.title: Company
about.lede: FastAccounts is an open-source bookkeeping product built for UK and Estonian small businesses and accounting bureaus.

sections.title: Legal entity
sections.body: FastAccounts is developed and operated by Predictive Labs Ltd, a company registered in England and Wales under number 14857334. Its registered office is 155 Minories Street, Suite 275, London EC3N 1AD, United Kingdom.

sections.title: Team
sections.body: A small Predictive Labs team maintains the product, documentation and public release history; Joosep Laats is named in the 0.3.0 release record for the merged product work. We do not present a larger team, customer count or adviser network than the evidence supports.

sections.title: Accounting-market competence
sections.body: Available: tested UK VAT and Estonian VAT (KMD) workpapers, country-specific invoices, exact Decimal tax calculations and immutable double-entry postings. Review required: independent UK and Estonian accountant UAT. FastAccounts is software, not tax or legal advice.

sections.title: Product boundary
sections.body: Available: invoices, bills, evidence, bank-statement import and reconciliation, ledgers, reports and reviewable VAT workpapers. Review required: Estonian payroll for accounting-bureau client books must complete production UAT. FastAccounts is not an ERP and does not include inventory, order management, manufacturing, CRM or general HR.

contact.title: Contact
contact.lede: One working inbox, with a clear subject line for each path. We do not publish mailboxes that are not configured.

sections.title: Sales
sections.body: Ask about the hosted Pilot, self-hosting or an accounting-bureau evaluation. Include your market, organisation type and the workflow you want to test.

sections.title: Support
sections.body: For product help, include the FastAccounts version, page or workflow, what you expected and what happened. Never send passwords, OAuth tokens, bank credentials or real accounting exports by email.

sections.title: Security
sections.body: Report a suspected vulnerability or incident privately. Include affected versions and reproducible detail, but do not include live credentials or unnecessary personal data.

sections.title: Data protection
sections.body: For account or service-data requests, state the organisation and data concerned. Requests about a client book should normally go first to the organisation that controls it.

terms.title: Terms: draft
terms.lede: These Pilot terms are placeholders, not final customer terms, and do not create claims about service levels, compliance or warranties.

sections.title: Service scope
sections.body: FastAccounts provides bookkeeping software and an optional hosted Pilot. Availability uses four labels: Available, Review required, Pilot and Planned. Direct tax filing is Planned and is not included unless a signed agreement expressly says otherwise.

sections.title: Customer responsibilities
sections.body: Customers remain responsible for accurate source data, user access, review of accounting and payroll outputs, statutory submissions and professional advice. Synthetic demonstrations must not be treated as production books.

sections.title: Open-source software
sections.body: The source repository is published under the MIT License. Self-hosted use is governed by that licence; operating, securing, backing up and updating a self-hosted deployment remains the operator’s responsibility.

sections.title: Hosted Pilot
sections.body: Pilot: availability, support, data processing, fees, cancellation and service levels for hosted use must be set in a separate customer agreement. This draft does not promise uninterrupted service, a response time or a production recovery objective.

sections.title: Legal terms still to be agreed
sections.body: Warranties, liability limits, governing law, dispute terms and a production data-processing agreement require legal review and are intentionally not fabricated here. Contact Predictive Labs Ltd before relying on the hosted service for live books.

landing.process_title: From bank statement to reviewed returns.
landing.process_body: A repeatable workflow for each client’s books. Explore it with synthetic data in the bureau demo.
landing.step1_body: Start with statement imports. Planned: read-only open banking; no provider is connected by default.
landing.step2_body: Keep invoices, bills and evidence together in each client’s books.
landing.step3_body: Review suggested matches and supporting evidence before confirming a posting.
landing.step4_body: Available: VAT workpapers and export. Planned: direct tax submission.

landing.old2: Payment matches explained in a separate spreadsheet.
landing.old3: Client books spread across disconnected folders.
landing.old4: VAT figures copied into another workbook.
landing.new1: Invoices, bills and evidence in one workspace.

landing.new3: Separate client books with a shared overview.
landing.new4: VAT workpapers to review before export.
landing.title: Open bookkeeping
landing.headline: Bookkeeping that stays clear, whoever keeps the books.
landing.lede: Run your own books or manage separate client books in one calm workspace. Review documents, reconcile payments and prepare UK and Estonian VAT workpapers with confidence.
landing.invoice_body: Country-aware invoices, credit notes, payments, reminders, and a complete receivables trail.
landing.reconcile_body: Import statements, match with evidence and documents, and review ambiguity before anything posts.
landing.review_body: VAT workpapers, ledgers, reports, evidence, audit history, and explicit filing-agent plans.
landing.hero_sub: A focused path for small businesses keeping their own books, and another for accounting bureaus managing many client books.
landing.hero_trust: Open source · UK and Estonia · Your books, your control
landing.audience_title: Choose the way you keep the books.
landing.audience_body: FastAccounts serves two distinct working models. Start with the one that matches your day-to-day responsibility.
landing.audience_bureau_body: Manage payroll, payables and bookkeeping across separate client organisations, with a clear review trail for each book.
landing.audience_business_title: I run my own business books
landing.audience_business_body: Issue invoices, record bills, reconcile bank activity and prepare VAT workpapers for one organisation.
landing.small_business_title: For small businesses running their own books
landing.small_business_body: Keep the everyday path focused: sell, record costs, reconcile cash and hand over reviewed records when you need professional help.
landing.suite_label: Each product has one job, with the same straightforward hosting choices.
landing.suite_fastmail_body: Business email for teams and client communication.
landing.suite_fastoffice_body: Documents and spreadsheets for everyday work.
landing.suite_fastmeet_body: Video meetings for teams and clients.
landing.suite_fasthr_body: Employee records, leave and people operations.
landing.suite_fastbooks_body: A lightweight financial overview for smaller teams.
landing.faq1_a: FastAccounts is open-source bookkeeping software for UK and Estonian small businesses and accounting bureaus. It brings invoices, bills, banking, ledgers and VAT workpapers into one workspace.
landing.faq2_q: What is the difference between BYOC and hosted?
landing.faq2_a: Bring Your Own Cloud (BYOC) is free: you run FastAccounts on your own infrastructure and manage updates. Hosting with us costs €1 per product per month on FastSME-managed infrastructure.
landing.faq3_a: Available: UK and Estonian bookkeeping plus VAT workpapers and export. Review required: Estonian payroll for accounting bureaus awaits production UAT. Planned: direct tax submission.
landing.faq4_q: Can I inspect the code and self-host?
landing.faq4_a: Yes. FastAccounts is available on GitHub under the MIT license. You can use, modify and self-host it under that license, retaining its copyright and permission notice.
landing.faq5_a: Available: employee file import and FastHR. Review required: QuickBooks Online, Xero, Merit Aktiva, BambooHR and Personio. Pilot: HMRC workpapers and Estonian KMD/VD export. Planned: direct tax filing, open banking and the remaining catalogue. No provider is connected by default.
landing.cta_title: Give every client's books a clear home.
landing.cta_body: Start with your workspace, or explore the source and host FastAccounts yourself.
